chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs73706717; association is linked or passenger
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TF binding at rs73706717 in HCT116.
Any 8q24 CRC signal is explained by a linked causal variant or by LD with a nearby variant such as rs6983267.
CRISPR allele swap at rs73706717 alone does not change enhancer activity or MYC expression.
falsified_if: A robust allele-specific TF binding and enhancer/MYC effect is seen at rs73706717 in HCT116.
CRISPR swap of rs73706717 alone changes MYC expression.
The effect remains after controlling for linked 8q24 variants.

chains.title: Alt C increases TCF7L2 binding at the 8q24 enhancer, raising MYC in HCT116 and promoting CRC

links.claim: The alt C allele creates or strengthens a TCF7L2/TCF4-family binding site in the 8q24.21 enhancer; TCF7L2 binds alt C more strongly than ref T.
This variant lies in an 8q24.21 enhancer element active in colorectal cancer cells; the alt C allele increases enhancer output.
The enhancer contacts and regulates MYC, so increased TCF7L2 binding at alt C raises MYC transcription.
HCT116 has active Wnt/TCF7L2 signaling and expresses MYC, making this enhancer-TF axis plausible in this cell line.
Higher MYC output in colorectal epithelium increases colorectal cancer risk or progression.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or EMSA shows alt C > ref T binding in HCT116.
An enhancer reporter in HCT116 shows alt C > ref T activity.
MYC mRNA is higher in cells carrying alt C at this element.
TCF7L2 knockdown reduces the alt-C-specific enhancer/MYC effect.
falsified_if: Alt C does not increase TCF7L2 binding in HCT116.
The allelic enhancer or MYC effect disappears after TCF7L2 knockdown.
The association is fully explained by a linked variant such as rs6983267.

chains.title: Alt C increases LEF1 binding at the same 8q24 enhancer, raising MYC in HCT116

links.claim: The alt C allele creates or strengthens a LEF1 binding site; LEF1 binds alt C more strongly than ref T.
The variant sits in an 8q24.21 enhancer and alt C increases its activity in colorectal cells.
Increased LEF1-bound enhancer activity raises MYC transcription.
HCT116 has Wnt/TCF-LEF activity and is a relevant colorectal cancer model.

predictions: Allele-specific LEF1 binding shows alt C > ref T.
LEF1 knockdown, but not TCF7L2 knockdown, reduces the alt-C enhancer effect.
TCF7L2 supershift/ChIP does not show the allele-specific binding.
falsified_if: LEF1 does not bind the element allele-specifically.
The allelic effect is TCF7L2-dependent rather than LEF1-dependent.
No enhancer or MYC effect is seen.

chains.title: Alt C alters CTCF binding at 8q24, changing enhancer-insulator topology and MYC
chains.element: 8q24.21 CTCF/insulator or enhancer boundary near MYC

links.claim: The alt C allele changes a CTCF binding site; CTCF binds alt C more strongly than ref T.
Altered CTCF binding changes insulator/boundary function at 8q24.21.
Changed boundary function alters MYC enhancer-promoter contacts and MYC expression.
HCT116 has CTCF-bound 8q24 architecture and expresses MYC.
Altered MYC regulation contributes to colorectal cancer.

predictions: Allele-specific CTCF ChIP shows alt C > ref T.
Hi-C or 3C in HCT116 shows altered MYC contact frequency.
CTCF knockdown or dCas9 boundary perturbation changes MYC.
falsified_if: No allele-specific CTCF binding is detected.
8q24 topology and MYC expression are unchanged.
TCF7L2/LEF1 binding explains the allelic effect better.

next_experiment: Allele-specific EMSA/oligo pull-down with HCT116 nuclear extract, using T and C probes, plus a TCF7L2 supershift or TCF7L2 immunodepletion. If alt C shows stronger TCF7L2-dependent binding, H1 is supported. If there is no reproducible allele-specific TCF7L2 binding, the null is favored and linkage/CRISPR testing is needed before claiming a TCF7L2 mechanism.
